title: Al-Ikhlas: sincerity
hook: say, He is Allah, One, the Eternal, unbegotten, none like Him (Surah 112)
tomorrow: Worth a third of the Qur'an

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-Falaq, the daybreak, and refuge in the One who splits the dark. Your line was lord of the daybreak. Day one hundred sixty-one.

In the car, with no warning, a child asks the biggest question there is: what is God like? Where did God come from? Who are God's parents? According to the commentators, people asked the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ questions like these. Describe your Lord to us. What is He made of? Where is He from? The answer came as one of the shortest surahs in the Qur'an. Four lines. It fits on an index card, and Muslim children often learn it right after al-Fatiha.
screen: `WHAT IS GOD LIKE?` → `DESCRIBE YOUR LORD TO US.` → `FOUR LINES.`

segments.voice: Here is Surah one hundred twelve, in Pickthall's translation: Say: He is Allah, the One! Allah, the eternally Besought of all! He begetteth not nor was begotten. And there is none comparable unto Him. You've heard its key word twice on this path, from Bilal on the burning sand, on day fifteen and day ninety-one. Qul huwa Allahu ahad. Arabic has two words for one. Wahid is one in a count, the first number. Ahad is one with no second at all: it can't be split, copied or added to. Then as-samad. Pickthall reaches for eternally Besought of all. Scholars give it layers: the one everyone turns to in need, who needs no one; the one who is complete, without a hollow. Then two denials: no children, no parents. God is not part of a family tree. And last: nothing is like Him, nothing you can picture, compare or draw. None of these lines says ikhlas. It means sincerity, or purity, the way you'd purify gold of anything mixed in. Scholars say the surah is named for what it does: it makes belief in the one God pure. That oneness is called tawhid, the center of Islamic belief. Jews and Christians also confess one God, and Christians understand that oneness through the Trinity; this surah is how Muslims say it, in their own four lines. And that closes a week: the stone lifted from the road, the close of the practices camp, then the text camp opening with hear it first, refuge first, and three surahs of refuge and oneness.
screen: `SAY: HE IS ALLAH, THE ONE.` · `AHAD — ONE WITH NO SECOND.` · `AS-SAMAD — NEEDED BY ALL.` · `NONE COMPARABLE UNTO HIM.` · then, large: `HE IS ONE.`

segments.voice: If you pray, you can recite the surah three times, slowly, qul huwa Allahu ahad, all four lines, with a breath between rounds. If you don't, let your mind reach for a picture of the biggest thing you know, the night sky, the ocean, the whole of time, and notice how fast it comes. Then remember the last line, none is comparable, set the picture down, and sit in the space it leaves.
Ahad. One, with no second: the oneness of Allah in the first line of Surah al-Ikhlas. Today's word.
Your line: he is one. One, with no second, and nothing mixed in. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Surah al-Ikhlas is among the first surahs Muslim children learn; it is recited often in the daily prayers, three times with al-Falaq and an-Nas morning and evening, and before sleep.

fork.setup: people come to the Prophet and say: describe your Lord to us. what answer comes?
options: a long list of names and deeds
four short lines: He is One, needed by all, unbegotten, beyond compare
fork.reveal: according to the commentators, Surah al-Ikhlas answered that request: one of the shortest surahs, and the center of Islamic belief.

original.note: Arabic: one, single, with no second; used of Allah in 112:1.

trapdoor: what you thought: ahad is just the word for one.
what it means: one with no second, undivided and beyond compare, the heart of tawhid.
what a scholar hears: ahad, not wahid, in 112:1; as-samad appears only here in the Qur'an and has several classical meanings.
